hero.support: Resomix is a reference-analysis and discovery tool for producers. It uses the PYXIS-1 analytical engine to examine 70+ musical characteristics across rhythm, harmony, timbre, structure and energy, then surfaces sonically related tracks that can unlock new production ideas.
hero.figureAria: The creative loop breaks open: a reference track feeds the PYXIS-1 sonic profile, five labelled dimensions, rhythm, harmony, timbre, structure and energy, fan out, and the highlighted thread reaches an unexpected sonic match: new directions to explore
hero.title: Understand your recording and study [[the music around it.]]

statement.bridge: You may already know the atmosphere, groove or energy you want. The difficult part is translating that feeling into the next production decision.
statement.inspiration: Inspiration is a powerful tool that often feels outside of our control. We have an idea for a track, where it should go, the atmosphere it should convey, but have no idea how to bring that vision to life. That's when we get stuck in an endless loop: unable to move forward, if not by ditching an entire project for a fresh start.
statement.pull: But what if you could start from a track that already captures that feeling, and use it as an inspiration to discover completely new creative directions?

block.h2: When you hit a creative block
block.opener: Creative block often appears as repetition: the same eight-bar loop, the same presets, the same sample choices and an arrangement that refuses to move forward.
block.engines: Discovery engines can help you expand your horizons and try something new, but the problem is that most of them are designed to help you find music based on what you already know and what they rely on: genre, artist names, tags, and so on. If you're looking for a specific atmosphere or sonic texture, it can be difficult to describe exactly what you want and results might not be what you need.
block.pull: Sometimes, the best way to find a new idea is to stop searching for exactly what you already have in mind, and start looking for more subtle connections in mood, atmosphere, and emotion.
block.figureAria: A rich sonic atmosphere drawn as layered contours and grain sits above typical discovery fields such as genre, artist and tags, which stay empty; the feeling cannot be typed into the form

paths.h2: Use the track that has the feeling to find what comes next
paths.intro: Start with a track that captures the feeling you want to pursue. PYXIS-1 examines the musical relationships behind that reference and surfaces related tracks through groove, energy, harmony, timbre and structure.
paths.engine: PYXIS-1 builds a sonic profile from the reference track across structural, harmonic, rhythmic, timbral and energy characteristics, then surfaces related tracks that can expand your field of reference.
paths.connections: Use those connections as material for study and contrast, then decide how they inform your own arrangement, sound design and production choices.
paths.listIntro: In short, here's how Resomix can help producers at any stage of their career:

stronger.label: Find stronger references
stronger.text: Start with the track that carries the feeling, then explore sonically connected music beyond familiar artists, genres and tags.

patterns.label: Break familiar patterns
patterns.text: Compare how other tracks express related groove, energy, texture or structure through different production choices.

connections.label: Discover unexpected connections
connections.text: Surface relevant tracks outside your usual scene, listening habits or reference library.

reinterpret.label: Reinterpret the signal
reinterpret.text: Transform what you discover through your own arrangement, sound design and production language.

craft.h2: PYXIS-1 surfaces the relationships. You shape the result.
craft.body: Resomix does not generate a track or prescribe a formula. PYXIS-1 surfaces relationships across rhythm, harmony, timbre, structure and energy. You decide what to study, reinterpret, contrast or leave behind in your own production. the story behind Resomix
craft.figureAria: A reference track feeds the PYXIS-1 sonic profile of 70+ characteristics; four labelled relationship branches lead to related sonic directions, and from the white-ringed result the producer's own white contour grows; analysis surfaces the connections and the producer makes the music

items.q: How do I analyse a reference track?
items.a: Upload it to Resomix and open Track Intelligence. You get structure, energy journey, tempo, key, loudness, timbre and spectral character, each read from the audio and shown with confidence where it applies.

items.q: Can I upload my own unfinished track?
items.a: Yes. It is processed privately, never used to train PYXIS-1, and deleted no later than 24 hours after upload or analysis.

items.q: What does Resomix measure in a track?
items.a: More than 70 audio characteristics across rhythm, harmony, timbre, structure and energy. Resomix's PYXIS-1 engine combines them into one sonic profile, which is what it compares when it looks for related music.

items.q: Does Resomix generate music or tell me what to change?
items.a: No. It surfaces relationships and evidence. What to study, reinterpret or leave behind stays your decision.

final.h2: Bring a reference. Find a new direction.
final.body: Search for or upload a track that captures the groove, atmosphere or energy you are chasing. PYXIS-1 builds its sonic profile and surfaces related music for you to explore.
